news.headline: A dart loaded with a GPS tracker: N.C. sheriffs office tests StarChase tech for high-speed chases
Massachusetts State Police features StarChase for NBC News

paragraphs: StarChase makes GPS technology products and services designed for law enforcement, including a vehicle mounted GPS launcher and a tracking app. A Spectrum News story republished on its site explains that once a pursuit begins, a deputy's vehicle launches a dart containing a GPS tracker to tag the fleeing vehicle. Data then goes to the agency's real time intelligence center, allowing officers to track the vehicle without an active chase. The company says the technology de-escalates high-risk events in probable cause and exigent circumstances and supports agencies at every level of law enforcement.

Its home page reports 50,000+ tags deployed, 20,000+ arrests made, and 0 injuries or fatalities. State and local agencies use it for cross-jurisdictional coordination and to bridge case building and real-time apprehensions. Task forces get certified less-lethal options for fugitive, narcotics, trafficking, and other special operations. The company also positions the technology for border security and national defense as well as everyday law enforcement.

The same news story, dated March 13, 2025, reports that the Forsyth County Sheriff's Office in North Carolina had that month added StarChase to its deputies' toolbox. A testimonial from Sgt. C. Robertson of the Lake County Sheriff's office says the agency has tripled its StarChase units over six years. StarChase plans to exhibit at IACP 2026 at booth 1184.

quote.text: StarChase was founded on a simple belief: deliver life-saving technology solutions that significantly reduce risk in high-risk situations.
